title: Add session detail sort options
body:
## Summary
This change adds device-persisted session-detail sorting so store users can choose how count items are ordered while working a session. The business goal is to reduce the cognitive overhead of preparing uploads just to control runtime list order and to make the in-app counting experience more flexible.

Closes #1392

## What changed
- adds `Uploaded order`, `Alphabetical`, and `Last updated` sort options on the session detail page
- persists the selected session-detail sort in the existing user-profile UI filter store on the current device
- stores `importItemSeqId` in local session records so uploaded order is stable and explicit client-side
- reuses the existing client-side sorting pattern already established around SmartFilterSortBar-style identity sorting
- documents the feature in app docs and adds spec/plan notes under `docs/superpowers`

## Testing
- `npm run lint -- src/stores/userProfileStore.ts src/composables/useInventoryCountImport.ts src/views/SessionCountDetail.vue src/services/commonDatabase.ts`
- `npx tsc --noEmit --pretty false --incremental false`
- verified in Chrome DevTools MCP on `http://localhost:8080/session-count-detail/M100168/DIRECTED_COUNT/M110470`
- confirmed default `Uploaded order` on first load
- changed sort to `Alphabetical`, reloaded, and confirmed persistence on the same device
- changed sort to `Last updated`, confirmed persistence, then restored the session back to `Uploaded order`

## Notes
- the sample session used for verification had only two uncounted items, so it was sufficient to verify control presence and persistence but not a visually dramatic reorder between modes
- hard-reloading an active session emitted an existing session-lock toast during testing; that behavior predates this change and was not introduced here

linkedIssues.body:
## What is the motivation for adding/enhancing this feature?

On the session detail page, store users should be able to sort items on device without depending on the import file being pre-arranged for them.

Today users are alphabetizing imports before upload because that is the only practical way to influence counting order once a session starts. The goal of this enhancement is to move that control into the app and reduce operator effort during counting.

## Approved scope

Add session-detail sort options for:

- Uploaded order
- Alphabetical
- Last updated

Persist the selected sort on the current device until the user changes it or clears app data.

## Implementation notes

- Reuse the existing client-side sorting patterns already established in `SmartFilterSortBar` where possible.
- Reuse the existing persisted Pinia `userProfile` UI filter pattern for device persistence.
- Do not introduce backend changes in this iteration.
- Use existing session item data to derive sort behavior.
- Treat `importItemSeqId` as the upload-order anchor in local session records.

## Sorting behavior

- `Uploaded order` should be the first-load default on devices with no saved preference.
- `Alphabetical` should follow the same user-facing identity logic already used in the app, preferring hydrated primary display identity and then falling back safely.
- `Last updated` should sort most recently changed rows first.

## Testing

Validate in the browser runtime that:

- first load defaults to `Uploaded order`
- changing sort updates the visible item order correctly
- the selected sort persists after reload on the same device
- grouped rows stay stable when switching between sort modes

## Summary

Add directive support in DSL for:
- field-level directives such as `@include` and `@skip`
- root mutation field directive `@idempotent`
- directives on inline fragments and fragment spreads

## Constraints
- keep implementation backward compatible with existing DSL snippets
- use overloads where needed to preserve existing call signatures

- verify generated GraphQL structure for include/skip/idempotent and fragment scenarios

title: Updated processBulkOperationResult to handle canceled Shopify operations
body:
Close: hotwax/mantle-shopify-connector#299

#### Problem
When a Shopify bulk operation is `canceled`, it does not provide a result URL. 

Previously, the polling service would error out when it tried to process a canceled operation because the URL was missing. Since the service errored out, the system message remained in `SmsgSent` status indefinitely. This caused the polling to get stuck on the canceled operation and blocked all subsequent bulk operations from running.

#### Solution
The fix is to handle the `canceled` status correctly. 

Now, when an operation is canceled, we set a `responseText` and update the message status. This allows the polling service to terminate correctly without erroring out. This unblocks the polling process so that other bulk operations in the queue can be processed.

title: Add jobOutput with sent message IDs to send#ProducedBulkOperationSystemMessage
body:
## Overview

Closes #308

Adds a `jobOutput` out-parameter to the `send#ProducedBulkOperationSystemMessage` service so that the IDs of all successfully transmitted system messages are recorded in the job output for auditability.

## Changes

### `ShopifySystemMessageServices.xml`
- Added `<out-parameters>` block with a `jobOutput` parameter
- Initialized a `sentMessageIds` list at the start of the action block
- After each successful call to `send#ProducedSystemMessage`, the processed `systemMessageId` is added to the list
- At the end of execution, if any messages were sent, the IDs are joined into a formatted string and set to `jobOutput`
  - Example output: `Sent system message IDs: [10001, 10002]`

## Notes
- The collection mechanism naturally supports future expansion if the service is ever updated to send multiple messages per run
- Early-return paths (operation already in progress, no messages to process) are unaffected and will not produce a `jobOutput`

linkedIssues.body:
### Overview
The "send bulk operation" job currently processes system messages but doesn't provide feedback in the job output about which specific messages were handled. To improve auditability and troubleshooting, the service should record the IDs of all successfully transmitted messages in the `jobOutput`.

### Proposed Implementation Design

#### 1. Target Service
The primary service responsible for sending bulk operations is `co.hotwax.shopify.system.ShopifySystemMessageServices.send#ProducedBulkOperationSystemMessage` (located in `mantle-shopify-connector`).

#### 2. Service Definition Changes
- **Add Out-parameter**: Define an out-parameter `jobOutput` of type `String`.
  ```xml
  <out-parameters>
      <parameter name=jobOutput/>
  </out-parameters>
  ```

#### 3. Service Logic Enhancements
- **ID Collection**: Initialize a list (e.g., `sentMessageIds`) at the start of the action block.
- **Tracking**: After each successful call to `org.moqui.impl.SystemMessageServices.send#ProducedSystemMessage`, add the processed `systemMessageId` to the list.
- **Output Formatting**: At the conclusion of the service, if the list is not empty, join the IDs into a comma-separated string and set it to `jobOutput`.
  - Example: `Sent system message IDs: [10001, 10002]`

#### 4. Concurrency Consideration
The service currently includes a check to prevent multiple bulk operations of the same type from running simultaneously. The implementation should ensure that even if only one message is sent (as per current logic), its ID is still recorded. If the logic is ever expanded to send multiple messages, the collection mechanism will handle it naturally.

### Expected Outcome
Technical stakeholders will be able to view the `jobOutput` field in the Service Job History to quickly identify the scope of a particular job run.

## Business summary

This PR adds a Gemini Code Assist style guide for `hotwax/oms` so automated code reviews can better match the review expectations Deepak Dixit and Anil K Patel have already established in OMS PR feedback.

The goal is to make automated review comments more useful for the team: less generic feedback, more checks around OMS-specific service contracts, REST shape, domain semantics, data placement, performance, concurrency, and code cleanliness.

title: Fail fast on historical order grouping failures to prevent rollback-only transaction reuse
body:
## Summary
When processing historical orders:
1. `syncShopifyOrder.groovy` called `co.hotwax.sob.order.ShopifyOrderSyncHistoryServices.create#ShopifyOrderSyncHistory` with `requireNewTransaction(true)`.
2. Inside `create#ShopifyOrderSyncHistory`, `co.hotwax.sob.order.ShopifyOrderServices.create#HistoricalShopifyOrder` was executed, which invoked `createHistoricalShopifyOrder.groovy`.
3. Inside `createHistoricalShopifyOrder.groovy`, when the `group#OrderByItemGroup` service call failed, `ec.message.clearErrors()` was used to swallow the exception and continue.
4. While this cleared the message facade's error state, the JTA transaction had already been marked as `ROLLBACK_ONLY`.
5. The script continued its execution without propagation, leading to a rollback at the end of the transaction scope.
6. The caller `syncShopifyOrder.groovy` was unaware of the failure because the errors had been cleared, so it proceeded to execute downstream database operations like `update#ShopifyOrder`.
7. Because the transaction was poisoned and rolled back, subsequent operations failed with database connection errors (`Error finding one OrderHeader`).

## Changes Implemented

### [Component: hotwax-shopify-oms-bridge]

#### [MODIFY] [createHistoricalShopifyOrder.groovy](file:///home/prerak/Project1/moqui-framework/runtime/component/hotwax-shopify-oms-bridge/script/co/hotwax/sob/order/createHistoricalShopifyOrder.groovy)
- Replaced the swallowing block with a fail-fast return to propagate the service error correctly up the stack, preventing downstream queries from executing against a poisoned transaction.

```diff
-            if (ec.message.hasError()) {
-                ec.logger.warn("Ignoring error running service group#OrderByItemGroup: ${ec.message.getErrorsString()}")
-                ec.message.clearErrors()
-            }
+            if (ec.message.hasError()) {
+                ec.logger.error("Error running service group#OrderByItemGroup: ${ec.message.getErrorsString()}")
+                return
+            }
```

## Log Work
- Hours spent: 10

## Issue Link
- Closes #143

**Error Details:**

title: Fallback to ReturnAgreement when RefundAgreement is missing
body:
Resolves #217

### Changes
- Updated the `refundAgreement` lookup in `syncShopifyOrder.groovy` to fall back to `linkedReturnAgreement` when `RefundAgreement` is missing.

### Why
This ensures we can still retrieve the app name (`refundAgreement?.app?.title`) and set the correct return channel instead of defaulting to the admin channel (`ADMIN_RTN_CHANNEL`) when Shopify only creates a `ReturnAgreement` for a refund.

linkedIssues.body:
### Problem
Sometimes Shopify does not create a `RefundAgreement` for a refund. Instead, it creates a `ReturnAgreement`.

Currently, in `syncShopifyOrder.groovy`, we only look for `RefundAgreement` using the refund ID. When it is missing, the `refundAgreement` variable becomes `null`.

### Impact
Because `refundAgreement` is `null`, we cannot get the app name (`refundAgreement?.app?.title`). This app name is needed to find the correct return channel. Since the app name was missing, the sync could not find the channel and defaulted it to `ADMIN_RTN_CHANNEL` (admin channel).

### Solution
Modify the lookup logic in `syncShopifyOrder.groovy`. If a `RefundAgreement` is not found, fall back to using the `ReturnAgreement` (which is already resolved as `linkedReturnAgreement` in the script).

```groovy
def refundAgreement = payload.refundAgreements?.find { it.__typename == "RefundAgreement" && it.refund?.id == refund.id } ?: linkedReturnAgreement
```

Closes #185

## Summary

- Adds a `createOrders` Boolean in-parameter (default `true`) to `co.hotwax.sob.order.ShopifyOrderServices.sync#ShopifyOrder`.
- When `createOrders=false` and the order has no `ShopifyOrderHistory` row, the service logs and returns instead of calling `create#ShopifyOrder`.
- Lets us split the MDM pipeline into two queues (create + update-only) backed by the same service, so new orders no longer wait behind the update backlog.

## Why this is safe

- Default is `true`, so any existing caller is unchanged.
- The early-return is placed only inside the `!syncHistory` branch — the historical-bootstrap block above still creates `ShopifyOrderHistory` rows for pre-launch orders, and the update branch and downstream fulfillment / refund / transaction processing are untouched.
- Because only the create queue is allowed to create orders, both queues running against the same Shopify order id cannot produce duplicates in OMS.

## Files changed

- [service/co/hotwax/sob/order/ShopifyOrderServices.xml](service/co/hotwax/sob/order/ShopifyOrderServices.xml) — new in-parameter.
- [script/co/hotwax/sob/order/syncShopifyOrder.groovy](script/co/hotwax/sob/order/syncShopifyOrder.groovy) — early return when `createOrders=false` and no sync history exists.

## Urgency

Marked urgent — current single-queue setup is causing order import latency in production.

## Test plan

- [ ] Call `sync#ShopifyOrder` with no `createOrders` param against a brand-new Shopify order id → order is created in OMS (default behavior preserved).
- [ ] Call with `createOrders=false` against a brand-new Shopify order id (no history row) → service logs the skip message and returns without creating an order; no `ShopifyOrderHistory` is written.
- [ ] Call with `createOrders=false` against an order that already has a `ShopifyOrderHistory` row → update branch runs as before (header/item updates, fulfillments, refunds, transactions all process).
- [ ] Call with `createOrders=false` against a historical order (createdAt before `newOrderSync.launchDate`) with no history → historical bootstrap creates the `ShopifyOrderHistory` row and the order proceeds through the update path.
- [ ] Configure both MDM queues in a non-prod environment and verify a fresh order created during the test flows only through the create queue (no duplicate creation from the update queue).

## Problem

The `syncShopifyOrder` service currently handles both order creation and order updates from a single MDM queue. New orders are stuck waiting behind a long backlog of update jobs, which is slowing down order import and breaking real-time processing expectations.

## Proposed change

Run two MDM queues against the same `syncShopifyOrder` service:

- **Create queue** — invokes the service with default behavior (`createOrders=true`).
- **Update queue** — invokes the service with `createOrders=false`.

Both queues share the existing logic, but the update queue is forbidden from creating new orders in OMS. This is critical: if both queues could create orders independently, we would risk duplicate orders for the same Shopify order id.

## Implementation

Surgical change to `syncShopifyOrder`:

1. Add a `createOrders` Boolean in-parameter (default `true`) to the service definition.
2. In the script's "no syncHistory" branch (the only path that creates an order in OMS), bail early with a log line when `createOrders=false`.

Behavior:
- Existing callers that don't pass the param keep current behavior (create + update).
- Update queue passes `createOrders=false`; if no `ShopifyOrderHistory` row exists for the order, it is skipped — the create queue will pick it up on its next pass.
- Historical-order bootstrap (orders with `createdAt` before `newOrderSync.launchDate`) still runs in both queues; downstream fulfillment / refund / transaction processing is unchanged.

## Urgency

Order import latency is impacting real-time processing. We need this in production ASAP.

## Summary
Refactor the Shopify order sync flow so `sync#ShopifyOrder` resolves `ShopifyShop` once and passes the required shop-scoped context into downstream focused services.

## Goal
Move shop-context ownership to `sync#ShopifyOrder` and stop reloading `co.hotwax.shopify.ShopifyShop` inside each focused service in the direct sync path.

## Problem
The current sync flow passes `shopId` into downstream services, and multiple services independently reload `co.hotwax.shopify.ShopifyShop` and revalidate the same shop context.

This creates:
- repeated shop lookup code
- repeated `Shopify Shop not found` validation
- unclear ownership of shop-context resolution
- noisy service boundaries

## Target Design
`sync#ShopifyOrder` should:
- validate `shopId`
- load `co.hotwax.shopify.ShopifyShop` once
- derive required shop-scoped values once
- pass resolved context into focused services directly

Focused services should:
- assume shop context has already been resolved by `sync#ShopifyOrder`
- not reload `ShopifyShop`
- not repeat shop-existence validation
- only perform checks relevant to their own mutation logic

## Context to Resolve Once in `sync#ShopifyOrder`
At minimum:
- `shopId`
- `productStoreId`

Additional context may be passed where useful:
- `shopifyOrderId`
- `orderId`

## Services in Scope
This task should cover the services directly involved in the refactored sync path:
- `sync#ShopifyOrder`
- `update#ShopifyOrderHeader`
- `sync#ShopifyNewOrderItems`
- any explicit sync-history services introduced for the new flow

Future quantity-sync work should follow the same pattern.

## Implementation Plan
1. Update `sync#ShopifyOrder`
- load `co.hotwax.shopify.ShopifyShop` once near the start of the flow
- fail early if shop is not found
- derive and store shared context values such as `productStoreId`

2. Define explicit focused-service contracts
- add explicit Moqui parameters for resolved context
- pass `productStoreId` directly where needed
- pass `orderId` and `shopifyOrderId` directly when already known

3. Update `update#ShopifyOrderHeader`
- remove internal `ShopifyShop` lookup
- remove internal `Shopify Shop not found` check
- accept resolved context from `sync#ShopifyOrder`

4. Update `sync#ShopifyNewOrderItems`
- remove internal `ShopifyShop` lookup
- remove internal shop validation
- accept resolved context from `sync#ShopifyOrder`

5. Apply the same rule to any explicit header/item history services introduced as part of the refactor
- do not reload `ShopifyShop` there if they are sync-only internal services

6. Keep only mutation-safety checks in focused services
Examples:
- order exists
- order is not terminal
- line item does not already exist before creation

## What Not To Do
- Do not reload `ShopifyShop` inside every focused service called from `sync#ShopifyOrder`
- Do not repeat `Shopify Shop not found for: ${shopId}` checks in those focused services
- Do not keep both orchestration-layer shop resolution and worker-layer shop resolution for the same direct sync path
- Do not hide shared context derivation inside each focused service

## Acceptance Criteria
- `sync#ShopifyOrder` resolves `ShopifyShop` once
- focused services in the sync path no longer load `ShopifyShop` again
- focused services no longer perform duplicate shop-existence validation
- required derived values such as `productStoreId` are passed explicitly from `sync#ShopifyOrder`
- focused services retain only mutation-safety checks relevant to their own work
- service parameter contracts are explicit and Moqui-style

## Notes
- This is a refactor of context ownership, not a behavior change
- Keep this limited to the direct sync path being refactored
- If a service is meant to remain reusable outside the sync path, that should be called out explicitly before deciding whether to remove internal shop validation

Rows in the `ProductUpdateHistory` entity are stamped with `shopId="01"`, but `ShopifyShop.shopId` for the configured Shopify connection is `"SHOP"` (and would be a real shop identifier in any multi-shop setup). As a result, any consumer that filters `ProductUpdateHistory` by the real `ShopifyShop.shopId` gets zero rows.

title: Fixed: Incorrect check to mark orders to completed status for cancelled Shopify orders during import
body:
Changelog: Fixed

## Summary

### Fixes
- https://github.com/hotwax/hotwax-oms/issues/479

### What was reported

Orders cancelled in Shopify before import were being marked as **Completed** in HotWax, while their items remained in **Created** state.  
Affected orders: M100014, M100015, M100016.

Shopify payloads show:
- `cancelledAt` present
- `closedAt` present
- `displayFulfillmentStatus = UNFULFILLED`

System error observed:
- `Status change not allowed from Completed to Cancelled`

---

### Root cause

The order status determination logic incorrectly used:

```groovy
if (order.closedAt || order.displayFulfillmentStatus == 'FULFILLED')
```

This caused:

* Any order with `closedAt` (including cancelled orders) to be marked as `ORDER_COMPLETED`
* Even when `displayFulfillmentStatus = UNFULFILLED`

As a result:

1. Order was first set to **COMPLETED**
2. Refund/cancellation flow attempted to move it to **CANCELLED**
3. Transition **COMPLETED → CANCELLED** is invalid
4. Order remained stuck in incorrect **COMPLETED** state

---

### Fix performed

Updated condition to:

```groovy
if (order.displayFulfillmentStatus == 'FULFILLED')
```

This ensures:

* Orders are marked **COMPLETED only when actually fulfilled**
* Cancelled but unfulfilled orders are not incorrectly completed

---

### Expected behavior

* Orders with:

  * `cancelledAt` present
  * `displayFulfillmentStatus = UNFULFILLED`
    → Should **NOT** be marked as `ORDER_COMPLETED`

* Such orders should:

  * Remain in **CREATED** initially
  * Transition correctly to **CANCELLED** via refund flow

* No invalid status transitions should occur

---


## Log Work
- Hours spent: 6

---

## Issue Link
- Closes hotwax/hotwax-oms/issues/479

title: Fix: Shopify exchange rate calculation in order payment preferences
body:
## Summary

Fixes #495

This PR corrects the currency conversion logic in `ShopifyOrderServices.java` that was causing massively inflated `OrderPaymentPreference` amounts when processing Shopify orders with multi-currency (e.g., MXN presentment / USD shop).

## Changes

### 1. Increased exchange rate precision (line ~1841)
- Changed `presentmentMoney.divide(shopMoney, 2, ...)` → `presentmentMoney.divide(shopMoney, 6, ...)`
- Prevents rounding errors during reverse conversion

### 2. Conditional multiply vs divide (lines ~4765-4787)
- Added `isShopifyRate` flag to differentiate Shopify-sourced rates from OFBiz `UomConversion` rates
- **Shopify rate** (presentment/shop): uses `amount.divide(exchangeRate)` to convert back to shop currency
- **UomConversion rate** (direct multiplier): continues using `amount.multiply(exchangeRate)`

## Before
`16,771.74 MXN × 17.89 = $300,214.15 USD` ❌

## After
`16,771.74 MXN ÷ 17.89 = $937.29 USD` ✅

linkedIssues.body:
## Description

When importing Shopify orders where the presentment currency differs from the shop currency (e.g., MXN vs USD), the `OrderPaymentPreference` max amount is calculated incorrectly, resulting in massively inflated values.

**Example:**
- `presentment_money` = 16,771.74 MXN
- `shop_money` = 937.29 USD
- Exchange rate calculated by system = 17.89 (presentment / shop)
- **Expected OPP amount**: $937.29 USD
- **Actual OPP amount**: $300,214.15 USD (16,771.74 × 17.89)

## Root Cause

In `ShopifyOrderServices.java`, the method `getTransactionAndCreateOrderPaymentPreference` uses `amount.multiply(exchangeRate)` to convert from the transaction currency to the order currency. However, the Shopify exchange rate represents `presentment / shop` (i.e., how many presentment units per 1 shop unit). Converting presentment back to shop currency requires **division**, not multiplication.

Additionally, the exchange rate is truncated to 2 decimal places during calculation, which introduces rounding errors.

## Affected Code

- `ShopifyOrderServices.java` line ~1841: Exchange rate calculation with scale of 2
- `ShopifyOrderServices.java` line ~4782: `amount.multiply(exchangeRate)` always used regardless of rate source

## Expected Behavior

When converting from presentment currency to shop currency using a Shopify-sourced exchange rate, the system should divide the amount by the rate: `16,771.74 / 17.89 = 937.29 USD`.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure a Shopify store with shop currency USD and enable a presentment currency (e.g., MXN)
2. Place an order in MXN
3. Import the order into HotWax OMS
4. Observe the OrderPaymentPreference max amount is inflated by the square of the exchange rate
linkedIssues.title: Bug: Shopify exchange rate incorrectly applied, inflating OrderPaymentPreference amount

title: Relax SYS_MSG_RMT relationship on ProductStoreEmailSetting to one-nofk
body:
## Summary

- Mirrors hotwax/ofbiz-oms-udm#363 in this repo.
- The `ProductStoreEmailSetting → SystemMessageRemote` relation here also uses `type="one"`, which makes OFBiz emit a hard SQL FK against a local mirror table that never holds rows. The authoritative `SystemMessageRemote` data lives on the Moqui side, so every insert that sets `systemMessageRemoteId` fails with a `SYS_MSG_RMT` FK violation.
- Switches `type="one"` → `type="one-nofk"` on the relation. Field and relationship stay; only the DB-level FK is dropped.

## Linked issue

- hotwax/ofbiz-oms-udm#362 — runtime reproduction, root cause, and rationale are documented there.

## Why this is safe

- The related entity is owned by Moqui — OFBiz can't reliably enforce this FK without continuously mirroring rows.
- Existence is validated at runtime by `UnigateServices.send#UnigateRequest` on the Moqui side.
- The Klaviyo UI in `hotwax/company` pins `systemMessageRemoteId` to the literal `UNIGATE_CONFIG`, so there's no path for arbitrary values.

## Follow-up after merge

On any environment that already ran the previous entity definition (i.e. has the FK in place), drop it once before redeploying:

```sql
ALTER TABLE product_store_email_setting DROP FOREIGN KEY SYS_MSG_RMT;
```

title: Fixed: Receipt feed to use OrderItem externalId as lineId instead of ShipmentItem externalId
body:
## Summary

Closes #224

The `generate#TransferOrderShipmentReceiptFeed` service was using `ShipmentItem.externalId` as the `lineId` in the receipt feed sent to NetSuite. After new changes, NetSuite expects this to be the **Transfer Order line ID**, which is stored as `OrderItem.externalId`.

## Changes

**File:** `service/co/hotwax/netsuite/TransferOrderServices.xml`

In the `generate#TransferOrderShipmentReceiptFeed` service, updated the item-level loop to resolve `lineId` from `OrderItem.externalId` via the following lookup chain:

```
ShipmentReceipt (shipmentId + shipmentItemSeqId)
    → OrderShipment  (entity-find by shipmentId + shipmentItemSeqId)
    → OrderItem      (entity-find-one by orderId + orderItemSeqId)
    → externalId     ← used as lineId
```

### Before
```xml
<set field="shipmentReceiptItemMap" from="[lineId:shipmentReceiptItem.shipmentItemExternalId,
    quantity:shipmentReceiptItem.totalQuantityAccepted, productId:goodIdentificationList?.first?.idValue]"/>
```

### After
```xml
<!-- Get OrderShipment using shipmentId and shipmentItemSeqId to resolve the corresponding OrderItem -->
<entity-find entity-name="org.apache.ofbiz.order.order.OrderShipment" list="orderShipmentList" limit="1">
    <econdition field-name="shipmentId" from="toShipmentReceipt.shipmentId"/>
    <econdition field-name="shipmentItemSeqId" from="shipmentReceiptItem.shipmentItemSeqId"/>
</entity-find>

<!-- Get OrderItem to retrieve externalId which is the NetSuite Transfer Order line ID -->
<entity-find-one entity-name="org.apache.ofbiz.order.order.OrderItem" value-field="orderItem">
    <field-map field-name="orderId" from="orderShipmentList?.first?.orderId"/>
    <field-map field-name="orderItemSeqId" from="orderShipmentList?.first?.orderItemSeqId"/>
</entity-find-one>

<!-- Set Shipment Receipt Item level details, using OrderItem.externalId as lineId (NetSuite TO line ID) -->
<set field="shipmentReceiptItemMap" from="[lineId:orderItem?.externalId,
    quantity:shipmentReceiptItem.totalQuantityAccepted, productId:goodIdentificationList?.first?.idValue]"/>
```

linkedIssues.body:
## Discription

The `generate#TransferOrderShipmentReceiptFeed` service currently sets the `lineId` in the receipt feed payload using `shipmentItemExternalId` (i.e., `ShipmentItem.externalId`).

**Affected service:** `co.hotwax.netsuite.TransferOrderServices.generate#TransferOrderShipmentReceiptFeed`  
**File:** `service/co/hotwax/netsuite/TransferOrderServices.xml`

```xml
<!-- Current mapping -->
<set field="shipmentReceiptItemMap" from="[lineId:shipmentReceiptItem.shipmentItemExternalId,
    quantity:shipmentReceiptItem.totalQuantityAccepted, productId:goodIdentificationList?.first?.idValue]"/>
```

NetSuite script is updated to expect the `lineId` in the receipt feed to correspond to the **NetSuite Transfer Order line ID**, which is stored as `OrderItem.externalId` in OMS now.

## Changed Behavior
The `lineId` in the receipt feed must be sourced from `OrderItem.externalId` (the NetSuite line ID stored on the order item), resolved by navigating:

```
ShipmentReceipt (shipmentId, shipmentItemSeqId)
    → OrderShipment (shipmentId, shipmentItemSeqId)
    → OrderItem (orderId, orderItemSeqId)
    → externalId  ← use this as lineId
```

## Solution

In the `generate#TransferOrderShipmentReceiptFeed` service, for each `shipmentReceiptItem`:

1. Use `entity-find` on `OrderShipment` with `shipmentId` and `shipmentItemSeqId` to find the corresponding order shipment.
2. Use `entity-find-one` on `OrderItem` with `orderId` and `orderItemSeqId` from the result.
3. Use `OrderItem.externalId` as the `lineId` in the receipt feed payload.

title: Implemented complete test suite to validate communication gateway
body:
# Unigate Test Suite

This test suite ensures that Unigate's **TenantAuthFilter** and **CommGateway** (email communication) are working correctly after refactoring.

## Running the Suite

From the repository root:

```bash
./gradlew :runtime:component:hotwax-unigate:test
```

## Test Classes

### 1. UnigateAuthTests

Tests the `TenantAuthFilter` servlet filter in isolation using Spock mocks. Each test creates a fresh tenant and API key and then clean them up.

| Test Case | What It Checks |
|-----------|---------------|
| `missing_headers` | Request with no `api_key` or `tenant_Id` headers → 401 with "Missing authentication headers", filter chain not called |
| `invalid_key` | Request with a wrong `api_key` → 401, filter chain not called |
| `tenant_mismatch` | Valid `api_key` but wrong `tenant_Id` → 401, filter chain not called |
| `valid_auth` | Correct `api_key` and `tenant_Id` → filter chain is called (request passes through) |

### 2. CommGatewayTest

Tests the email communication gateway end-to-end using Moqui services. Creates a shared tenant, Klaviyo auth config, and Mayur auth config.

**Negative Scenarios:**

| Test Case | What It Checks |
|-----------|---------------|
| `invalid commGatewayAuthId` | Non-existent auth ID → error "No valid gateway auth config found for tenant" |
| `missing commGatewayAuthId` | No auth ID provided → error "Field cannot be empty (Comm Gateway Auth ID)" |
| `missing email` | No email address → error "Field cannot be empty (Email Address)" |
| `missing subject` | Null subject → Klaviyo returns 400 with regex validation error |
| `special characters in string field` | Special characters in `orderName` → no framework error, handled gracefully |
| `missing brandName` | Mayur email without `brandName` → 500 with NullReferenceException from the gateway |

**Positive Scenarios:**

| Test Case | What It Checks |
|-----------|---------------|
| `mail to Klaviyo` | Full payload with addresses, items, adjustments → Klaviyo returns 202 (or 401 if key invalid) |
| `mail to Mayur` | Full payload to Mayur gateway → 200 with success response |
| `without addresses` | Payload without facility/shipping/billing addresses → still succeeds (200/201/202) |


##  Before Running — Klaviyo API Key Required

The `CommGatewayTest` sends real requests to the **Klaviyo Sandbox API**. You must provide a valid Klaviyo sandbox public key before running the suite.

Open `CommGatewayTest.groovy` and replace the placeholder:

```groovy
publicKey: "<ENTER_KLAVIYO_PUBLIC_KEY>"
```
Without this, the Klaviyo tests will return `401 Unauthorized`.

---

### Viewing the Report

After the test run, open the HTML report in your browser:

```bash
open runtime/component/hotwax-unigate/build/reports/tests/test/index.html
```

This report shows pass/fail status, test output, and error details for each test case.
